summary: Phase 147D designed the implementation architecture for AEM-001 v1.0 (Phase 147B's frozen Authority Evaluation Model Contract, independently verified with two Non-Blocking findings at Phase 147C), documentation-only, no production code, test, contract, schema, or runtime file modified. Independently reconstructed implementation requirements from AEM-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, CHGR-001, PEC-001, TAMC-001/TAMPC-001, and GAC-001 primary text plus direct re-inspection of src/pcae/interactive_workflow/models/session.py, src/pcae/interactive_workflow/publication_handoff/{models.py,handoff.py}, src/pcae/governance/publication/{coordinator.py,record.py,models.py}, src/pcae/interactive_workflow/persistence/repository.py, tests/test_phase_144c_publication_coordinator.py's AST-enforced forbidden-import boundary, and the CHGR schema family (decision_template.schema.json, human_governance_record.schema.json). Concluded AEM-001's own evaluation mechanism -- a new, self-contained pcae.authority_evaluation package (EligibleAuthorityDeclaration and AuthorityEvaluationOutcome models, a pure evaluation function, an AuthorityRegistry ABC mirroring SessionRepository's own ABC-then-filesystem-implementation precedent from Phase 143K/145D) -- can be architected and, in a future phase, built with zero required modification to IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001's own owned files. Separately found that making that mechanism's output actually reach a published CHGR requires two further, separately-governed contract-revision phases (an IWC-001 minor revision widening PublicationReadinessPackage/Session, mirroring Phase 144F's own IWC-REQ-185 precedent for decision_maker_identity_evidence, and a PEC-001-conforming change to record.py consuming the widened Package's new field), neither of which is authorized by AEM-001 itself (which explicitly declines to redefine IWC-001/PEC-001) or by this phase -- disclosed as Finding FA-147D-1, the chapter's central architectural finding, refining rather than contradicting Phase 147A Sec.6.5's originally-projected phase sequence. Reconciled F-147C-1 (the dormant, free-text eligible_authority field already present in decision_template.schema.json) by retaining it entirely unchanged (no schema modification authorized) and assigning it, architecturally, the citation-source role AEM-REQ-026/Sec.7 and human_governance_record.schema.json's own authority_basis_claimed field description already imply ("citing the template's own eligible_authority field") -- the new, additive frozenset[str]-based eligible_identities set is a distinct, machine-evaluable membership construct serving a disclosed, non-overlapping purpose; a non-blocking drift risk between the two is named (Finding FA-147D-3) as an operational-discipline recommendation for a not-yet-existing future Decision Template authoring workflow, not mechanically closed, mirroring AEM-001 Sec.4.4's own no-policy-language judgment call. Also named a Registry-unavailability failure mode AEM-001's own text does not address (Finding FA-147D-2), distinct from AEM-REQ-010's None-for-no-Declaration case. Produced a full component architecture (six submodules under pcae.authority_evaluation: models, evaluation, registry, errors, serialization, plus a deferred concrete filesystem Registry implementation design), lifecycle-integration walkthrough (authority evaluated exactly once, upstream of Confirmation at the earliest point template_ref/template_version/claimed_identity are all available together; merely carried, never re-evaluated, through Confirmation/Readiness/Publication/CHGR generation/Verification/Inspection), failure architecture, security architecture (all eight AEM-001-inherited security properties hold; one disclosed, unclosed circular-trust gap restated unchanged from AEM-001 Sec.4.7/D-7), migration/incremental-rollout architecture, and test architecture (unit/adversarial/lifecycle/compatibility test shapes named; publication/integration test shapes named but explicitly not written, since they would exercise not-yet-governed cross-contract behavior). Zero Blocking findings. Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION ARCHITECTURE COMPLETE WITH OBSERVATIONS. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147D_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE.md.
